items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: you know. Same thing with Mose. On the other hand Mose Allison was known as a blues guy

ctx.x: Well the first thing, like I tell my students in the university, the first thing you have to do as a bassist or a rhythm section player, I think it’s true you know, chord players — pianists, guitarists, drummers, but especially the bass player. You have to be a really, a good listener you know. But then you have to have a repertoire. I mean you have to know a lot of songs, a lot of tunes, a lot of patterns you know. I was fortunate when I first started playing around Buffalo there was a piano player named JAMAN.…

you know. Same thing with Mose. On the other hand Mose Allison was known as a blues guy but he played very little traditional — I mean it always had the blues feeling, a heavy blues feeling, which really was remarkable, you know, especially for a white musician. I think he’s from Mississippi or somewhere like that. But he had this real nice, and he was an excellent pianist too actually. All of his music, it had chord changes. It had charts. When you listened to it, it sounded oh yeah he’s playing his blues, but…
